findings.evidence: `public section` at line 39 without `@[expose]`; Mathlib exposes bodies with `@[expose] public section` (mathlib/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Shapes/Pullback/Pasting.lean:34). Same repo convention: TauCeti/Probability/Recurrent.lean:69-79 adds `recurrent_def` because "the body is not exposed"; TauCeti/Topology/UniformlyLocallyConnected.lean:104 "downstream modules cannot [unfold], the definition being public but not exposed". Basic.lean:53 likewise provides `isEffectiveCartier_iff`.
findings.fix: Add the unfolding/intro interface: `theorem isRelativeEffectiveCartier_def (I : X.IdealSheafData) (f : X ⟶ S) : I.IsRelativeEffectiveCartier f ↔ I.IsEffectiveCartier ∧ Flat (I.subschemeι ≫ f) := Iff.rfl` (or an explicit `IsRelativeEffectiveCartier.mk` taking the two hypotheses).
findings.issue: `IsRelativeEffectiveCartier` is a `def ... : Prop` in a plain `public section`, so its body is unexposed downstream, and the file exports only the eliminators `.isEffectiveCartier` and `.flat`. No consumer outside this file can prove the predicate for a divisor it builds (e.g. ModularCurves' divisors of sections), only destructure one it already has.

findings.evidence: Mathlib gives both projections for every analogous iso: `comapIso_hom_fst` and `comapIso_hom_snd` (mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Functorial.lean:53,216, the latter landing in `subschemeMap _ _ f (I.le_map_comap f)`), and `pullbackRightPullbackFstIso_hom_fst/_snd/_inv_fst/_inv_snd_*` (mathlib/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Shapes/Pullback/Pasting.lean:465-493). `le_map_comap` is at Functorial.lean:127, `subschemeMap` at :206.
findings.fix: Add `@[reassoc (attr := simp)] theorem relativeBaseChangeSubschemeIso_hom_fst : (I.relativeBaseChangeSubschemeIso f g).hom ≫ pullback.fst (I.subschemeι ≫ f) g = subschemeMap _ _ (pullback.fst f g) (I.le_map_comap _)` (or, if preferred, the `≫ I.subschemeι` form equal to `(I.comap (pullback.fst f g)).subschemeι ≫ pullback.fst f g`), plus the corresponding `inv` lemma.
findings.issue: `relativeBaseChangeSubschemeIso` is characterized only by its composite with `pullback.snd (I.subschemeι ≫ f) g` (line 76). A morphism into a pullback needs both projections; with the def body unexposed, no consumer can relate the iso to `pullback.fst _ g` (the map to `I.subscheme`) without unfolding it.

findings.issue: `relativeBaseChangeSubschemeIso` and `relativeBaseChangeSubschemeIso_hom_snd` are general facts about `IdealSheafData.comap` and pullback pasting: their statements mention no effective-Cartier or flatness notion and their proofs use none. Under a `relativeBaseChange*` name in an `EffectiveCartierDivisor/Relative.lean` file, this general infrastructure is undiscoverable for the non-divisor uses it serves.

summary: The relative predicate exports only eliminators with an unexposed body, so downstream modules cannot introduce it at all, and the new comparison iso is characterized on only one of its two projections and lacks the simp annotation its Mathlib analogues carry.
